transit.name: Core Transit Leadville Route
transit.detail: Morning northbound and evening southbound service. Serves Vail, Minturn, Red Cliff and Leadville. Fare required to or from Leadville.

nameOrigin.text: The U.S. Geological Survey says the name was probably chosen because lead was the major mineral in both the placers and the lode mines.

founded.text: The city of Leadville was founded in 1878

timeline.text: August R. Meyer built the Greek Revival clapboard house now called Healy House.
Horace Tabor built the Tabor Opera House in 100 days.
Horace Tabor bought the Matchless Mine on Fryer Hill on July 17 for $77,850.
The Victorian school building that now houses the National Mining Hall of Fame and Museum dates to 1899. It was once Leadville's high school.

sites.name: National Mining Hall of Fame and Museum
sites.cost: $20 combo ticket with the Matchless Mine; Lake County residents free

sites.name: Matchless Mine Historic Site
sites.season: Opens for the season typically Memorial Day and closes for the season typically Labor Day

sites.name: Healy House Museum & Dexter Cabin
sites.hours: Gift shop and exhibit hall: Friday–Sunday, 10:30 am–2:30 pm

sites.name: Tabor Opera House
sites.season: Public group tours run from late May to the middle of October, Friday through Sunday
sites.cost: Private tours $40 per person or $100 per group of 4; free for children 10 and under

makers.name: Melanzana
makers.what: Outdoor apparel made locally in Leadville since 1994

trails.name: Mineral Belt Trail
trails.length: About 11.6 miles round Leadville (the County also gives 12), climbing 859 feet; 12 feet of pavement, at 9,897 to 10,637 feet
trails.trailhead: The dirt lot at the base of Dutch Henry Hill on U.S. 24 south of downtown; also Ice Palace Park, Community Park, and East 5th and East 7th streets
trails.season: All year: walked and ridden in summer, groomed for Nordic skiing and snowshoeing in winter; nothing is posted yet on 2026–27 grooming.
trails.dogs: On a leash no longer than 10 feet, under county law; pick up the waste.

trails.name: Mount Elbert trails
trails.manager: U.S. Forest Service, Leadville Ranger District
trails.length: North Mount Elbert Trail 4.3 miles one way, 4,400 feet up; South Mount Elbert Trail 5.8 miles, 4,800 feet up; the summit is 14,433 feet
trails.trailhead: North: U.S. 24 south 3 miles, Colorado 300 west ¾ mile to County Road 11, just west of Elbert Creek Campground. South: County Road 24 above Twin Lakes
trails.season: In winter the north trailhead’s road is for snowmobiles, hikers and skiers only; the south trail is the standard winter route. COTREX shows a Willow Fire closure at the north trailhead.
trails.dogs: Allowed; on the Forest’s trails outside its leash areas, dogs need no leash but must be under your control.
trails.fee: None at the north trailhead; commercial and organized groups need a Leadville Ranger District permit.

trails.name: Turquoise Lake Recreation Area
trails.manager: U.S. Forest Service, Leadville Ranger District
trails.size: 780 acres of water for recreation, with eight campgrounds of 300 sites and two boat ramps
trails.address: In the forest west of Leadville. Turquoise Lake Road (County Road 4) is barricaded from the Abe Lee turnoff to Hagerman Pass; use County Roads 9C and 9
trails.season: Facilities close in winter for ice and snow, and it is a popular ice-fishing lake; the 2026 boat ramps ran May 1 to September 7. The Willow Fire closure covers the forest south of the lake.
trails.dogs: On a leash in the developed campgrounds, picnic and day-use areas.
trails.fee: Day-use areas and campgrounds charge fees; fishing needs a Colorado license.
